transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-21 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Oliver (Zenith Head of ML), Sofia (Zenith Data Eng), Ankit (Zenith Security), Marie (Zenith Product)

00:00 Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll kick off, we're super excited to scope this POC for multilingual summarization and NER across your financial reports. quick agenda: success criteria, workload sizing, model shortlist, benchmark plan, and next steps.
00:28 Oliver: sounds good. quick context: we ingest earnings calls, regulatory filings, and internal analyst notes. need high quality extractive+abstractive summaries and entity extraction for regulatory entities, counterparties, monetary values. multilingual covers en/es/fr/de, english is ~70% of traffic.
00:47 Sofia: current infra is mostly on-prem with a GCP presence, we have a Kafka stream and a microservice that calls a hosted LLM endpoint today (expensive), so main drivers are cost, latency, and data controls.
01:05 Ankit: security-wise SOC 2 is a must, SSO via SAML, ability to keep audit logs and KMS integration for keys. we may require VPC/private deployment for some environments.
01:20 Diego: noted, Redwood supports hosted, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem). for the POC we usually start on hosted or dedicated depending on latency needs; we can simulate dedicated capacity during benchmarks.
01:35 Marie: success criteria from product: summaries should have >0.75 ROUGE-L against our refs, NER F1 >0.85 for named entities, and latency under 300ms 95th for single-request summarization if possible. cost target is TBD but we want to understand unit economics.
02:02 Maya: great, let's capture that as north-star. Mia - sorry i mean i misread - Diego will own the benchmark run, we'll aim for those thresholds. can you walk us through typical payload sizes and QPS?
02:18 Sofia: typical request is 200-800 tokens input, average 350 tokens, outputs 50-150 tokens. Batch of 1 for low latency, but some offline bulk runs too. steady-state about 12 QPS, spikes up to 60 QPS during earnings windows. monthly volume ~1.2M generated tokens.
02:50 Diego: ok that's helpful. for latency-focused POCs we look at 95th pctl at target concurrency. if you need <300ms 95th we may need dedicated GPU pools or smaller models with quantization. we should test both accuracy and latency tradeoffs.
03:10 Oliver: for domain accuracy financial terminology is critical — models need to handle monetary entities precisely. multilingual performance is a requirement not optional.
03:25 Priya: on model shortlist — based on your constraints and preference for open models, we'd propose testing: Llama-2-13B (base and 13B instruct/quantized), Mistral-7B-v0.2 (and instruct variant), and a 13B Q4HF quantized variant if available. optionally Falcon 40B could be included but it's heavier and likely higher cost/latency.
03:50 Sofia: curious about quantization — will it impact entity extraction accuracy?
03:56 Diego: short answer: sometimes, depends on quantization recipe. we usually compare Q4_K and int8/4 variants. for many NER tasks the drop is modest but we need to validate on your labeled set. that's why the benchmark includes quality metrics.
04:18 Marie: and on hallucinations — we need strict hallucination reduction for regulatory excerpts, any recommendations?
04:25 Priya: strategies: prompt engineering with retrieval/grounding, smaller context windows with relevant docs, and n-best reranking. Redwood supports hybrid routing where we can route to higher-quality variants for sensitive requests.
04:45 Ankit: network — if we run hosted, are there guarantees on data residency and retention?
04:50 Maya: hosted keeps tenant isolation; retention policies configurable, we have enterprise SLAs, and if you need VPC/on-prem we can do Redwood Private with customer-managed KMS. we'll send the SOC 2 summary and security whitepaper.
05:05 Oliver: timeline — we want a 2-week POC: week 1 ingest and bench set up, week 2 run benchmarks and review. is that realistic?
05:15 Diego: yes, two weeks is tight but doable if Zenith provides labeled samples quickly. Diego outlines benchmark plan: set up Redwood test workspace, ingest sample docs, run latency tests (cold vs warm cache), run quality evals (NER F1, ROUGE-L over summaries), and produce a tradeoff matrix.
05:40 Diego: we'll measure: p95 latency at target concurrency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, and quality metrics per language. we'll also test quantized variants and warmed KVS (prefix caching) effects.
06:00 Sofia: what's the expected infra footprint for the test? can you simulate Dedicated on hosted?
06:06 Diego: we can create a reserved-demo pool to emulate Dedicated throughput; for true Dedicated we need billing/commit, but for POC we often simulate. the bench will run on our high-perf instances and we can record metrics that map to expected Dedicated sizing.
06:25 Oliver: model selection question: between Llama-2-13B and Mistral-7B, which tends to be better for multilingual finance?
06:32 Priya: Llama-2-13B tends to have robust instruction-following and decent multilingual coverage; Mistral is strong in many benchmarks and has very good inference efficiency. for finance domain you often see fine-tuning or retrieval augmentation helps more than raw model choice. the bench will show actual deltas.
06:55 Marie: any red flags on latency with 13B quantized?
07:00 Diego: with q4_k quantization you can often hit low latencies on a single A10/A100-like GPU; 95th might still be higher than small 7B unless you do batching. continuous batching improves throughput but hurts tail latency. we'll include both metrics.
07:25 Ankit: about audit logs and SSO — can logs be forwarded to our SIEM and do you support SAML + SCIM?
07:32 Maya: yes to both; logs can be streamed to your SIEM, and we support SAML for SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. we'll include docs.
07:45 Sofia: for the benchmark dataset — we'll provide 200 samples balanced across languages with ground truth NER tags and reference summaries; some docs are scanned PDFs, OCR noise included. any tips for the OCR noise?
07:58 Priya: include OCR variants in the sample; we recommend a small cleanup pipeline but it's also good to benchmark with realistic noisy text. modeling approach: retrieval + rerank helps reduce errors from noise.
08:20 Diego: benchmark specifics: run these model configs
- Llama-2-13B (fp16)
- Llama-2-13B (q4_k)
- Mistral-7B-v0.2 (fp16)
- Mistral-7B-Instruct (q4_k if available)
- optionally Falcon-40B-lite for a high-quality baseline if time permits
We'll record per-language quality and latency.
08:55 Oliver: for scoring summaries do you use ROUGE-L only? can we add human spot checks?
09:00 Diego: automated ROUGE-L + semantic embedding similarity is our default; we recommend a small human spot check set for hallucinations and pragmatic quality. we'll budget for a 20-doc human review.
09:15 Marie: cost modelling — can Redwood give rough cost estimates for each config?
09:21 Maya: yes we'll provide unit economics: cost per 1k tokens for each model/config, and estimated monthly cost for your volume. that'll be in the pricing template.
09:30 Sofia: what about model rollouts and fallback policies? if a model is overloaded, can requests be routed to cheaper/higher-latency variants?
09:36 Priya: yes, Redwood supports smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible model variants by policy; you can set cost vs latency priority per route.
09:50 Ankit: encryption at rest and in transit? KMS options?
09:54 Maya: TLS in transit and customer-managed KMS for keys at rest with HSM integrations for Private deployments. we'll include specifics in the security pack.
10:10 Diego: ok i'll enumerate bench steps: ingest + preprocess, run warmup (cache priming), run latency sweep (1-60 QPS), quality eval per language, quantization comparison, and produce a report with tradeoff matrix. expected deliverable: benchmark report + recommended model for production and suggested Dedicated sizing.
10:40 Oliver: which model do you expect to recommend normally?
10:43 Priya: typically for this workload we see a sweet spot with Llama-2-13B-instruct when accuracy matters; Mistral-7B often wins on cost/latency tradeoff. final call depends on your labels.
11:00 Maya: timeline recap: Maya sends security docs + pricing by 2026-08-23; Zenith shares labeled samples by 2026-08-24; Diego runs benchmark and shares results by 2026-08-28; follow-up review week of 2026-08-31.
11:25 Marie: sounds good. one more operational question: can we get per-route token-level cost breakdown in the console?
11:30 Maya: yes Redwood Console provides per-route token cost and latency breakdowns, plus traces and error analysis.
11:40 Sofia: ok thanks everyone.
11:42 Oliver: thanks, Maya, Diego. looking forward to the report.
11:45 Maya: great, we'll get started. bye all.
